prompts.name: Orbital Dockyard
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: detailed visual mockup for an existing voxel space-station game model.
Input image 1 is the authoritative rendered Wayfarer model and governs the geometry and shape. Input image 2 is gameplay context only and establishes the six services and tiny player scale; remove ALL of its HUD, text labels, borders, and buttons.
Primary request: show a convincingly richer, more detailed version of THE SAME WAYFARER STATION. Preserve its recognizable architecture exactly: single tiered cylindrical/octagonal central command tower, open octagonal perimeter ring with small service pavilions, radial bridges and big empty fly-through quadrants, FOUR broad rectangular blue solar wings in paired sides, projecting foreground docking apron, rear cargo platform. Preserve the ivory/navy/copper/cyan/amber palette and the relative layout. Add designed functional details onto this structure, do not replace its silhouette with a different station.
Style: premium cohesive voxel game art, visibly assembled from crisp tiny cubic blocks, stepped edges and pixel surface materials, flat rectangular glass. High-quality ambient occlusion, soft directional light, subtle cyan and amber emission, substantial shadows. Do not make smooth photorealistic sci-fi or rounded conventional high-poly geometry.
Composition: one large full station, high three-quarter isometric camera matching image 1, fully visible with comfortable margins, on quiet very dark midnight blue space with a few tiny stars. Station occupies about 80% of the image. A tiny player craft close to the foreground apron clearly establishes monumental scale. Strong legible large forms; medium detail clusters with quiet surfaces between, microdetails only tertiary. Deep fly-through voids must stay unobstructed. No enormous background planet, lens flares, thick fog, UI overlays, leader lines, text, labels, titles, borders, watermark, collage, or repeated stations. Landscape presentation image.
Direction: WORKING ORBITAL DOCKYARD. Make the original Wayfarer feel operational and engineered with restrained industrial detail.
Add a pair of small voxel gantry service cranes beside the launch apron, recessed docking clamp sockets, segmented runway markings and guide lights, a partially open hangar door with a warm lit workshop and spare craft inside on the near right service pavilion. Add compact fuel couplings and parallel copper conduit runs under the rim, grouped stacked cargo containers and a loading arm on the existing rear cargo platform, boxy dark cooling vents and radiator fins below the ring. Detail the central command tower with layered armor panel insets, narrow maintenance balconies, antenna masts and a small stepped radar dish. Solar panels gain visible cross-bracing, cell segments, power boxes and hinge housings. Place a few tiny service drones and a tug near the apron. Selective yellow/black hazard stripe voxels only at docking points. Clean, maintained industrial wear, no rust apocalypse. Preserve all large shapes and the exact station identity.

Direction: LIVED-IN HOME PORT. Make the original Wayfarer feel welcoming, inhabited, and layered while retaining its functional space-station shape.
Give the existing service pavilions varied small upper floors, recessed warm window clusters, roof equipment and tiny observation balconies. Add two compact block-built glazed hydroponic greenhouses fitted onto existing ring segments, visible tiny voxel greenery behind cyan-tinted square glass, without enlarging the ring or filling its open quadrants. A few ivory modular cabin pods tuck underneath the perimeter with lit window bands. Add a glass-fronted lounge terrace on the central command tower, a small amber-lit maintenance gallery and a short blocky communications array. Make the foreground launch apron inviting with precise cyan landing lanes, berth number markings as small geometry rather than readable text, grouped luggage/cargo crates and a parked tiny craft. Distinguish the flight school pavilion with three compact blue practice beacons outside the ring. Inset utility panels, cable channels, door frames and rooftop cooling boxes supply close-up detail. Keep blue solar wings and ivory/copper shell dominant. Warm amber interior lighting against cool space. No trees outside sealed glass, no exposed human people in space, no fantasy castle or city replacing the station.

Direction: FRONTIER OBSERVATORY. Evolve the original Wayfarer into a precise exploration and research outpost with richer instruments and strong service identity.
Add a compact nested voxel observatory/radar assembly on the existing central tower roof, with a stepped dish, directional sensor mast and a few slender box antennas, preserving the tower height hierarchy. Route-map pavilion gains a recessed luminous cyan star-chart table visible through square glazing; archives on the rear platform gains protected ivory/navy data-vault cabinets with small violet status pixels and tidy cable conduits. Fit two short mechanical telescope barrels and sensor packages to ring service roofs, scale much smaller than the command tower. Under the rim add dark ribbed radiator banks and modular instrument drawers. The hangar pavilion has a recessed bright service portal and docking clamp arms; the launch apron receives fine inset amber approach strips and clear layered docking plates. Solar wings gain exposed segmented cell patterns, hinges and compact cable boxes. Small scanner drones and navigation buoys orbit nearby, with one tiny player ship by the front apron. Recessed mechanical detail, crisp panel seams, restrained cyan-violet instrument lights complement warm windows. Keep the whole original ring layout and its four panels; do not convert the station to a giant telescope or redesign the silhouette.
